headline: I Just Spent Three Weeks Defending A 'Strictly Decorative' Missile Defense Shield I Installed In My Living Room
body:
When my neighbor complained about the giant, rotating radar dish I bolted to my balcony, I had to be very clear: it is purely for aesthetic purposes and carries no aggressive intent whatsoever. Much like certain international treaties, my home-defense apparatus is purely symbolic, designed to complement my mid-century modern furniture rather than actually intercept anything coming from the kitchen or the hallway.

I’ve had to issue five formal clarifications to the Resident Welfare Association already, emphasizing that the surface-to-air paint job on the projectile tubes is strictly meant to reflect light during the golden hour. When they pointed out that the radar keeps making a 'locked-on' beeping sound whenever the courier arrives with a pizza, I explained that it’s simply a high-fidelity doorbell upgrade that just happens to track movement with military-grade precision.

It’s exhausting being so misunderstood. People see a sophisticated hardware installation and immediately jump to conclusions about intent, ignoring the fact that it matches my curtains perfectly. I told the society secretary that if he’s so worried about 'aggressive elements,' he should look at the neighbor’s aggressive leaf blower, which is clearly a weapon of mass irritation. As for me, I’ll just keep my defensive posture, which currently involves sitting on my sofa, sipping tea, and pretending my balcony isn't bristling with hardware that could theoretically defend the building from an incoming low-orbit satellite.
